Anya Patel: heads-up — after the rope_theta default tweak in the rollout, we're seeing intermittent KV-cache stalls + kernel selection thrash on llama3-13b in prod. sample trace attached. any ideas?

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T09:04:02Z by @anya to cluster-gpu-pool-3 succeeded (images: runtime:v3.14)

Perf dump: 

  GPU 0: kernel_selector: tried [fused_gemm, fast_gemm, fallback_gemm] for layer 45, selected fallback_gemm -> 72ms
  KV cache: miss-rate spike ~ 7% on warm prefixes
  batching: avg tokens/batch dropped 18% (chat template requests increased)

Jonas Müller: can you paste the kernel_selector logs and a flamegraph link? sounds like selector cooldown or the cost model got skewed by changed sequence-length distribution.

Anya Patel: paste: ```
[2026-03-18T09:03:59Z] kernel_selector: layer=45 candidate=[fast_gemm(est=18.2ms), fused_gemm(est=16.5ms), fallback_gemm(est=20.1ms)]
[2026-03-18T09:03:59Z] kernel_selector: selected=fallback_gemm reason=memory_pressure_estimate
[2026-03-18T09:03:59Z] kv_cache: evict_policy=LRU threshold=0.85 current_usage=0.88
[2026-03-18T09:04:00Z] batcher: emitted_batch_size=6 avg_expected=9
```
flamegraph: https://perf.internal/runs/2755551234/fg.html (sampling + nvprof)

Maria Chen: hunch: rope_theta tweak increased effective positional freq, so head/hidden alignment changed and some fused kernels no longer match expected tile shapes. selector falls back when workspace estimate > threshold. also small batches from chat templates amplify per-token overhead. try bumping kernel_cooldown_ms and lowering workspace_safety_margin; also verify head_dim parity (64 vs 80) for fused path.

Kevin O'Rourke: quick A/B: forced fast_gemm for layer 40-48 on a canary — latency down 14% p50, tail unchanged. cfg applied: ```
kernel_selector.forced_layers = [40..48]
kernel_selector.force = "fast_gemm"
batcher.min_batch_tokens = 12
kv_cache.max_shards = 8
```
results: p50 86ms -> 74ms, p95 312ms -> 305ms. not perfect but confirms selector misestimate.

Anya Patel: interesting. perftrace also shows low_utilization windows right before the fallback decisions — maybe the cost model uses peak-mem estimate that spikes due to temporary KV prefetching. we saw kv_cache evict events right before fallback.

Jonas Müller: action items: 1) add telemetry for estimated vs actual kernel runtimes (per-kernel error histogram) 2) experiment with reducing workspace_safety_margin from 1.2 -> 1.05 for Llama3 variants 3) patch selector to prefer kernels that historically had lower error for that model/hidden_size/head_dim combo

Maria Chen: also add a rule in routing: if avg_batch_tokens < min_batch_tokens and model_family=llama3 then prefer smaller-workspace kernels (avoid fused paths) — chat-template workload will keep showing up.

Anya Patel: I'm going to run a short canary with: rope_theta=0.5 (previous), workspace_safety_margin=1.05, kernel_cooldown_ms=500, and forced_layers for the hot range. will post numbers in ~30m.

perf-bot: scheduled profile run 2755551245 (anya-canary-2026-03-18) queued on cluster-gpu-pool-3

Kevin O'Rourke: one more note — check RMSNorm vs SiLU effects on compute pattern: for 13B we saw fused_norm_gemm path only triggers when rmsnorm_enabled && head_dim % 64 == 0. if recent tokenizer/chat-template padded inputs changed head alignment we can lose that fused path.

Anya Patel: good call. our deployment toggled rmsnorm=true for the rollout. I will try rmsnorm=false for the canary too.

Jonas Müller: thanks — if canary improves, we'll prepare a selector patch to use model-profile fingerprints (model_name + hidden_size + head_dim + rmsnorm_flag) to bias kernel scoring.

Maria Chen: :thumbsup: keep notes of kv evict timestamps, we need to distinguish prefetch eviction vs steady-state churn.

Anya Patel: noted. posting results shortly.

Kevin O'Rourke: fyi — if we hit repeated fallback due to memory estimate, we should consider a soft-evict/compact path in KV that reduces transient peak memory but preserves hit-rate. worth a follow-up RFC.

Anya Patel: RFC ack. moving to canary now — will update when perf-bot returns numbers.
